title: Enterprise Intake Matrix: SLA-driven Prioritization for Hosted API Feature Requests
creator: Marco Diaz
description: Create an SLA-driven intake matrix and prioritization rubric for enterprise-hosted API feature requests (chat, streaming, tool/function calling, structured outputs). Goal: standardize responses to sales and solutions engineering, reduce cycle time from request → scoping → roadmap decision, and provide transparent handoff artifacts for Eng/Design/Security. This ticket produces the matrix, three canonical triage workflows, and the internal playbook for handling urgent enterprise asks.
acceptance_criteria: A scoring matrix that maps request attributes (customer size, SLA need, PII/regulatory, integration complexity, revenue delta, strategic alignment) to a priority band and recommended path (quick patch, backlog, dedicated pilot, dedicated capacity).
Three documented triage workflows (chat streaming request, tool/function calling integration, structured-output contract) with decision gates and owner handoffs.
One-page playbook for Sales/SE to use when collecting intake info (fields + minimum attachments).
A sample fast-track approval template for P0 enterprise requests that includes security checklist, cost estimate, and rollback plan.
Matrix and playbook uploaded to Confluence and linked from hosted-api intake form; stakeholders (Eng leads, Security, Solutions Eng) have reviewed and provided signoff.
decisions: Use a weighted scoring model where SLA requirements and regulatory risk each carry 25% of the score; revenue & strategic alignment 20%; integration complexity 15%; maintenance burden 15%.
Introduce a 'Pilot Lane' for top-10 strategic enterprise customers that bypasses standard backlog but requires a 90-day sunset/roll-forward review.
Fast-track (P0) approval requires 2x engineering micro-commit estimate, SE acceptance, and security checklist completion; no fast-track without a named sponsor from Sales or Customer Success.
risks: Risk of over-promising latency/availability guarantees to enterprises when hosted capacity is constrained; mitigated by explicit fallback model variants andTraffic Shaping policy in the playbook.
Increased operational burden if many pilot lanes are opened without formal sunset rules.
Potential conflicts between fast-track customers and Dedicated capacity sales motions; need coordination with Revenue Ops.
